source.title: Current GP element sets, Active satellites, CSV

model.name: NRLMSIS 2.1
model.conditions: equator, local noon, quiet geomagnetic field (Ap 4)

checks.name: every satellite has one catalog number and a real orbit
checks.detail: no duplicate catalog numbers; periods above 80 minutes; perigees above 100 km

checks.name: 24-hour satellites sit at the textbook geostationary altitude
checks.detail: 568 satellites with a day-long period; median altitude 35,787 km (textbook 35,786 km)

checks.name: space station altitude matches NASA's published orbit
geostationary light time works out to about half a second
model air density at sea level matches the standard atmosphere
air at 400 km is about a trillion times thinner than at sea level
checks.detail: 2.1e+11 times thinner at moderate solar activity

checks.name: the thermosphere really is hot
checks.detail: up to 1,429 K (1,156 C) at high solar activity

checks.name: above 400 km the air delivers under 1% of what sunlight does
checks.detail: worst case 3.40 W/m2 against 1360 W/m2 of sunlight

checks.name: orbit bands add up to the catalog
radiator budget is in the expected range
checks.detail: 679 to 1592 W/m2 net at 30 to 90 C; worst-case shadow 37% of the orbit
